1.summary: Shoyo Hinata spends junior high practicing volleyball mostly alone, then finally gets a team together for one official tournament by borrowing friends from other clubs. They face powerhouse Kitagawa Daiichi and lose in straight sets to its setter, Tobio Kageyama, the "King of the Court". Hinata vows to beat him at Karasuno, the school of his idol, the Little Giant.

290.summary: The Inarizaki match comes down to its last, exhausting rallies, with both teams throwing everything they have left at each other, until Karasuno battles its way to match point.

369.summary: Karasuno's third-years graduate in a few quick panels, closing the team's first Nationals run. The chapter then jumps forward several years, ending the high school story and setting up the time skip.

370.summary: Five years later, Yachi, now in college, fills in what happened to Karasuno: the team placed third at Nationals in Hinata's third year, with Yamaguchi as captain and Hinata in the number 5 jersey. Kageyama went pro and Yachi, Yamaguchi and Tsukishima went to college, while Hinata left for Brazil to learn beach volleyball. The chapter ends with Hinata watching Kageyama play for Japan at the 2016 Rio Olympics.

371.summary: A flashback to Hinata's first months in Rio de Janeiro shows how rough the move was: training goes worse than planned, his wallet is stolen and he cries alone in his room. He slowly makes friends and earns the nickname "Ninja Shoyo", and at a beach pickup game he runs into someone speaking Japanese: Toru Oikawa.

372.summary: Flashbacks to Aoba Johsai reveal that Oikawa planned to play overseas, and that the setter who inspired him now plays for Argentina's national team. In the present, Hinata texts Kageyama a selfie with Oikawa, and Kageyama silently shows it to his teammate Ushijima.

375.summary: Hinata keeps polishing his beach game with his partner Heitor, and the two talk about what volleyball means to each of them as they build toward a real tournament match.

376.summary: Hinata and Heitor play a beach volleyball match against Carvalho and Santos. They grab an early edge in the third set, but they have to outlast a far more experienced and technical pair to win.

377.summary: Hinata returns to Japan after his time in Brazil, more mature but aware he still has things to learn. Bokuto reappears, Atsumu turns out to be on the same team, and the chapter closes on Hinata helping a teammate up at the end of a match.

378.title: The Final Boss
378.summary: A few months later, Hinata is officially a member of the MSBY Black Jackals. Most of the old Karasuno team gathers to watch his first match against Kageyama, and the two former partners finally meet again, face to face, before the game.

379.summary: The V.League match between the Black Jackals and the Schweiden Adlers is about to start, and the stands fill with familiar faces: Ukai, Takeda, Karasuno alumni and Shiratorizawa's old players. In the bathroom Hinata meets Sakusa and jokes with the pros, it turns out Tanaka and Kiyoko are married, and Tanaka breaks down in tears when Hinata walks onto the court.

380.summary: The Great Monster War finally begins. Hinata's first receive calls back to an old exchange with Kageyama, and Shiratorizawa's former coach Washijo arrives to watch the match.

381.summary: Atsumu sets Hinata with the same pinpoint precision Kageyama used to, and Bokuto echoes something Akaashi once said about the freak duo. Akaashi and Hinata's idol, the Little Giant Tenma Udai, appear in the crowd, a flashback looks at the Miya twins, and Japan's national team coach is watching.

382.summary: Ushijima's serve blows through the Black Jackals' libero, so the Jackals switch to a total-defense setup that recalls Karasuno's plan against Shiratorizawa. Atsumu and Hinata's quick catches the Adlers' coach off guard, and Bokuto's serve sets the crowd roaring.

383.summary: Hinata aims his serve to take Brazilian star Romero out of the play, but Romero digs it and turns the motion into a spike that surprises Kageyama. Romero praises Kageyama's set, and Hinata, Bokuto and Atsumu all react with jealousy.

384.summary: Hinata shows how far his receiving, once his weakest skill, has come in Brazil. He slips in and out of the opponents' view to fake them out as a decoy, surprising Kageyama and the Adlers, while Daichi works out his trick from the stands.

385.summary: Hinata sets the ball for Atsumu, proof of the all-around game he built on the beach. In the stands, Tsukishima, Yamaguchi and Yachi explain why the Jackals picked him over a bigger, more experienced player, and the chapter ends with the score at 21–17.

386.summary: Nishinoya, who has been missing from the reunion, is shown fishing in Italy. On court, Hinata makes an overhead receive, Bokuto saves a ball with a chest receive, and Hinata ends the chapter with a spike that turns into a fake quick set.

387.summary: This chapter is all about Kageyama. Flashbacks show him learning volleyball from his grandfather and older sister, idolizing Oikawa in middle school, and practicing alone after pushing his teammates away, a lonely path that mirrors Hinata's.

388.summary: Kageyama shows off his pro skills with a one-handed set and a fake set that recall Oikawa, while Hinata keeps baiting blockers as a decoy. Bokuto keeps a rally alive after being blocked, and Kageyama grudgingly notices how stable Hinata's balance has become.

389.summary: Kageyama remembers how free and trusted he felt at Karasuno. Tsukishima notices that he is using the sides to stretch the Jackals' block, Bokuto struggles to keep up, and Kunimi and Kindaichi reveal that Kageyama will move overseas next year.

390.summary: Atsumu takes the spotlight and reminds Kageyama that Hinata is not the only Jackal he has to worry about. He debuts a new deceptive serve that borrows the motion of his jump float for a jump serve, fixing the predictability that hurt him in high school.

392.summary: A Bokuto chapter. It reveals that Fukurodani reached the Spring Nationals final and finished second, with Bokuto's last spike blocked, and shows Bokuto's reaction to ending up on the same pro team as Atsumu.

393.summary: The Adlers fight back on the scoreboard and nearly level the set, and the chapter ends with the Black Jackals clinging to a 20–19 lead.

394.summary: Adlers outside hitter Korai Hoshiumi takes over the scoring, using his huge jump to make up for his height. The Adlers find new ways to deal with the Jackals' cross-court spikes and read through Bokuto's block-out trick.

395.summary: A flashback shows Ushijima, frustrated by his losses as a pro, meeting Iwaizumi in California, where Iwaizumi studies sports science and shows him clips to help him. Tendo also returns. In the present, Ushijima's new arm swing brings the score to 24–23.

396.summary: It is revealed that Kageyama's grandfather and Coach Washijo were both Shiratorizawa alumni, and the chapter looks back at how Hinata's meeting with Hoshiumi and Kamomedai lit his hunger to improve.

397.summary: Atsumu keeps landing serves that break through the Adlers, putting the Black Jackals ahead 11–9 with Hinata, Bokuto and Sakusa all contributing. On the Adlers' side, Hirugami praises Hoshiumi's work, and the stage is set for Hinata against Hoshiumi.

398.summary: In the fourth set, the chapter zooms in on a single receive. Ushijima keeps attacking and Hinata keeps stopping him, while flashbacks to his old failures and Ukai's comments show how much his balance and stance improved in Brazil.

399.summary: The fourth set grinds on as Hinata and Ushijima try to prove who is better, and the chapter starts showing each player under a banner with their old high school motto, beginning with Hoshiumi.

400.summary: The last points of the Great Monster War arrive at match point. Hinata goes for a minus-tempo quick, Kageyama reads it and is already waiting, and the chapter ends with both of them going for the ball under a single "Fly!" banner as the crowd splits its support.

401.summary: The Black Jackals win the match, and Bokuto, not Hinata, scores the final point after Hinata draws the defenders away as a decoy. Kuroo returns in a suit, working for the Japan Volleyball Association, Kageyama tells Kindaichi and Kunimi he wants to play with them again, and the chapter ends with Hinata and Kageyama in Japan's national team uniforms.

402.summary: The final chapter shows Japan, with Hinata and Kageyama, facing Oikawa's Argentina at the Olympics, without revealing the winner. It then jumps a year ahead to the World Championships and checks in on the rest of the cast, from Tendo and Ushijima to Asahi and Nishinoya traveling abroad together.
